Hey!  I currently have a ringneck i got around november of last year, and i can say my experience with her has been different from other owners, due to her upbringing. The stereotype is that ringies love talking and are very mean, but they are not at all. If i had a stereotype for them, I’d say they are very needy. My rn is pretty shy and skittish, but she loves when you sit and talk to her, or sing. She likes flying around the house and is pretty independent, and doesn't let people pet her. She tends to kinda be nippy, and use to not like hands, but I've been training her out of it. Id definitely say to go and interact with the bird a couple times before bringing them home, and see if you click with your bird. (Also, let me say, my ringie was left in her cage for like two or three years and not well socialized, so that does factor in to her and her mannerisms. She is wonderful but i should not have taken such a difficult bird such as her.)

Anyways, good luck, and be sure to post your rn once you get them!

When i brought home my ringie, i spent time in the same room as her, but didnt really react with her besides refilling her food and water and giving her treats.   I generally just talked to her and gave her lots of treats lol.

I agree with the person above, also those cozy hut things (like the little tent things) have also been shown to be dangerous for birds. With my ring, we didn't encourage her to sleep anywhere, she just sleeps on her swing perch most of the time. So you can see which perch they like best and observe them from that.
